article.title: Metro DC DSA Condemns Councilmember Christina Henderson’s Attempted Power Grab and Disregard for DC Home Rule
article.author: Metro DC DSA
article.content: Metro DC DSA Condemns Councilmember Christina Henderson’s Attempted Power Grab and Disregard for DC Home Rule Date: November 8, 2026 Media Contact: For all press inquiries, please contact media@mdcdsa.org . Washington, DC: Metro DC Democratic Socialists of America condemns At-Large Councilmember Christina Henderson’s cynical attempt to manipulate the District’s Home Rule laws for her own political advantage, undermining the democratic process and distracting from the urgent challenges facing working-class Washingtonians. Details: In 2020, Henderson switched her party affiliation from Democrat to independent to run for an At-Large Council seat. Now, following Councilmember Robert White’s resignation, Henderson attempted to reverse that decision, potentially depriving the DC Democratic Party of its authority to appoint an interim replacement and shifting that power to the DC Council. When the DC Democratic Party moved to exercise its appointment authority, selecting Jamal Holtz before Henderson’s registration change took effect, Henderson raised the prospect of legal action. Only after her maneuver failed did she reverse course and re-register as an independent. Analysis: Home Rule is not a political tool to be invoked when convenient and discarded when inconvenient. It is the foundation of the District’s limited right to govern itself, a right generations of Washingtonians have fought to secure against congressional interference. Henderson’s actions have all the appearances of a naked political power grab, seemingly designed to strengthen her position for a potential challenge to the Council chairmanship. Whatever her ambitions, Washingtonians deserve better than elected officials exploiting party registration rules to advance their political careers. This spectacle is particularly offensive at a moment when DC residents face an escalating affordability crisis. Working families are struggling with rising rents, the cost of groceries, and underfunded public services. Instead of addressing these urgent needs, Henderson has manufactured a political controversy over who gets to fill a temporary vacancy on the Council. The timing could hardly be worse. As the District enters a new political era, with renewed threats to our autonomy and an expanded National Guard presence in our streets, our elected officials should be demonstrating the seriousness and resolve necessary to defend DC residents against federal interference. Instead, Henderson’s political maneuvering makes our local government appear unserious, irresponsible, and consumed by personal ambition. Bottom Line: The irony of Henderson invoking Home Rule to defend her actions should not be lost on anyone. The District’s right to self-government belongs to its residents, not to politicians seeking to manipulate the rules for personal advantage. The DC Democratic Party’s authority to appoint an interim replacement is established under District law, and voters will have the opportunity to elect their next At-Large Councilmember in a special election. Metro DC DSA supports respecting the established appointment process while reaffirming our commitment to full DC statehood, which would eliminate the undemocratic congressional restrictions on our local government that helped create this controversy. Councilmember Henderson should abandon these political games and return her attention to the people she was elected to serve. Washingtonians need leaders fighting for affordable housing, strong public schools, fully funded public services, and genuine democratic self-determination, not politicians more interested in their next promotion than the needs of their constituents. Our city deserves a government that takes itself seriously, respects the will of its voters, and puts working people first.
